# Scope and Evidence Contract

This supplement documents one retrospective CRPTO specification audit. The
archive had been inspected during earlier project iterations. The active
protocol was committed before its complete run, but it is not a prospective
trial, preregistration, or pristine lockbox. The inferential object is the
finite Lending Club archive under the declared information, outcome, policy,
and comparator contracts.

The audit reports every eligible consecutive six-month residual window and five
protocol-locked coverage specifications. The primary detailed audit retains CatBoost and
numeric logistic, while monotonic CatBoost and two WOE/IV scorecards broaden
model-class coverage checks; only the primary CatBoost enters optimization. The
coverage record has three deliberately separate layers: sharp finite-archive
identification bounds, a retrospective joint-block combined-rank reference
diagnostic, and outcome-isolated sensitivities for timing and calibration
taxonomy. The missingness-encoding, individual-age second-origin,
label-Mondrian, and closed four-map CatBoost calibrator families are complete
sensitivities rather than selection grids. The calibrator family uses one
common uncalibrated-probability ($q_{\mathrm{raw}}$) taxonomy, reports every
map and cell, and performs no optimization; only the pre-existing Platt score
enters the separate primary portfolio analysis. The decision audit reports the
complete five-point gamma path, two rulers constructed
without policy-development or OOT evaluation outcomes, three interior coordinates,
and every comparator in each named support. *Evaluation-outcome-blind* means that
earlier model and conformal fitting may use historical labels, while policy
construction reads neither development nor OOT evaluation outcomes. The
nine fixed-cap policies remain a supporting registered-cap diagnostic, not a
closed family of promotion candidates. No out-of-time (OOT) outcome selects a
learner, window, taxonomy, gamma, ruler, coordinate, policy, cap, or comparator.
Nested supports, overlapping windows, and repeated allocations are
specification paths, not independent replications or votes.

| Reader question | Location | Audit answer |
|---|---|---|
| Which loans could enter a decision? | Appendix A | Status-independent monthly menus retain unresolved outcomes |
| What does the conformal object predict? | Appendix B | The observed binary terminal label, not latent individual PD |
| Why can interval geometry change abruptly? | Appendix B | An exact rank-count condition can switch which mirror calibration sample supplies the binary residual order statistic |
| What is held fixed in portfolio comparisons? | Appendix C | Menu, budget, payoff, loan bounds, purpose cap, solver, and one declared ruler |
| What is exact? | Appendices B and D | Mirror-order-statistic threshold geometry, the crossed-band coverage identity, score-ruler algebra, C2 feasibility, binary-outcome bounds, and the conditional within-basis endpoint lemma |
| Which empirical signs survive? | Appendix E | The endpoint sign changes by ruler/coordinate and no sign survives the finite registered cap values spanning $[0.05,0.12]$; continuous-support extrema are not computed |
| Can the evidence be replayed? | Appendix F | Yes, conditional on authorized access to the hash-identified raw and DVC inputs, using the active source registry and full raw-data audit |
| What may the paper claim? | Appendix G | Finite-archive facts and joint-block rank-reference flags at locked nominal thresholds, not significance, superiority, causality, or selected-set validity |
| How does CRPTO differ from its closest methods? | Appendix H | By its frozen-score audit target, not by claiming each component as new |

: Reader map for the Online Supplement.

# Appendix A: Data, Timing, and Outcome Observability

## A.1 Single status-independent universe

<!-- claim:data.exhaustive_status_independent_population -->
<!-- claim:endpoint.not_verified_snapshot -->

The source is a locally verified Lending Club 2007--2020Q3 research extract.
The audit establishes the local file's identity and contents, not its
acquisition history or redistribution rights. A chunked full-file audit reads
all 2,925,493 rows and 142 columns; 2,925,492 are
valid dated loans. The archive contains 2,060,077 36-month and 865,415 60-month
contracts. The single active design retains all 640,543 loans eligible under
deterministic schema, date, term, and origination-feature checks. It is an
exhaustive design population, not a sample or row cap. Candidate membership
never depends on whether the reconstructed endpoint is resolved.

The decision unit is issue month. Every OOT month receives a fresh USD 1
million budget, and a policy can allocate only to loans issued in that month.
The primary panel contains 376,890 candidates in 15 menus from April 2016
through June 2017. A July--September 2017 extension contains 88,227 candidates
and is retained only as a more heavily censored diagnostic.

| Block | Issue dates | Rows | Labels available by cutoff | Role |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| PD development | 2007-06--2010-12 | 17,433 | 17,392 | model fit and temporal validation |
| Platt calibration and taxonomy | 2011-01--2011-12 | 14,101 | 14,077 | separately fitted score map and fixed edges |
| Residual pool | 2012-01--2013-01 | 49,007 | 48,857 | all eight six-month recipes |
| Policy development | 2013-02--2013-12 | 94,885 | not read | outcome-free comparator support |
| Primary OOT | 2016-04--2017-06 | 376,890 | read only after freeze | complete locked evaluation |
| Censored extension | 2017-07--2017-09 | 88,227 | read only after freeze | secondary censoring stress |

**Table S1.** Chronology and label observability. Blocks do not overlap except that the eight residual windows overlap by design.

The information cutoff for model and residual labels is March 31, 2016. The
evaluation endpoint cutoff is September 30, 2020. The distributed file is not
a verified point-in-time snapshot: 36,485 last-payment dates and 40,214
last-credit-pull dates occur after that cutoff. A charged-off residual
label is treated as available at the month-end of `last_pymnt_d` plus six
calendar months; every included residual month retains more than 99% of
terminal labels under this
rule. The minimum monthly retention is 0.992956.

The complete audit explains why the remaining archive cannot be treated as
exchangeable extra training data without further assumptions. Forty-eight variables have negligible early support and
near-complete later support, so admitting them would change the temporal
feature contract. Label availability by the cutoff is 59,910/162,570 (36.85%)
for 2014, 28,878/283,173 (10.20%) for 2015, and 1,110/96,120 (1.15%) for
2016Q1, with zero observed bads in the last group. A resolved-only fit would
therefore select on duration. Sixty-month contracts define another horizon;
using censored cohorts coherently would require a survival or competing-risk
estimand rather than a larger binary sample. Type-I conformal survival methods
require the censoring time for every unit, while general right-censoring methods
require conditional independent censoring, positivity, and nuisance-model
contracts [@candes2023survival; @gui2024adaptive]. If
prepayment prevents later default observation, it is a competing event rather
than automatically independent censoring, and calibration would concern
event-specific cumulative incidence functions [@li2023online_loans]. None of
these results retrospectively identifies the binary endpoints used here.

For primary OOT, requested and funded amount differ by only USD 18,000 across
376,890 loans. The funded-to-requested ratio is 0.999996 and only about two
loans are partially funded. The optimizer nevertheless names listed loan
amount as its exposure contract rather than treating the two fields as
interchangeable by assumption.

## A.2 Endpoint taxonomy and censoring

<!-- claim:endpoint.reason_census_partitions_candidates -->

Statuses containing `Charged Off` are positive ($Y=1$), and statuses containing
`Fully Paid` are negative ($Y=0$), only when reconstructed endpoint availability
is no later than the cutoff. Exact `Default`, every nonterminal status, and
terminal statuses becoming available later remain unresolved. The primary
panel has 364,814 resolved and 12,076 unresolved candidates. Fully Paid is
available at the month-end of `last_pymnt_d`; Charged Off is available at that
month-end plus six calendar months. The charge-off delay is a modeling
assumption, not the known operational charge-off date. The exact reason census
is:

| Reconstructed endpoint reason | Candidates | Resolved | Unresolved |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Fully Paid by cutoff | 307,842 | 307,842 | 0 |
| Charged Off by cutoff | 56,972 | 56,972 | 0 |
| Nonterminal or otherwise unresolved | 11,551 | 0 | 11,551 |
| Terminal after reconstructed cutoff | 47 | 0 | 47 |
| Terminal availability date missing | 478 | 0 | 478 |

**Table S1A.** Endpoint-reason partition of all 376,890 primary candidates. The last two rows sum to 525 but represent different observability failures.

This endpoint is a cutoff-specific terminal classification, not a lifetime hazard.
The analysis does not assume that unresolved outcomes are missing at random.
Instead, allocations are frozen first and each unresolved binary outcome is
allowed to take either value in sharp fixed-allocation and paired-policy
bounds. This preserves the historical menu while exposing the uncertainty
that outcome filtering would conceal.

## A.3 Physical information boundary

Prediction, residual-recipe construction, policy development, comparator
support, point-frontier enumeration, and allocation freezing run without OOT
status, status-indexed payoff, miscoverage, or another outcome-derived field. The
outcome-free phase persists 51,117 solve records and 5,001,617 funded rows. It
contains 1,872 guardrail solves: eight windows by nine policies by 26 monthly
menus, of which 11 are development and 15 are primary OOT. It also contains
1,080 OOT C2 solves: eight windows by nine policies by 15 months.

The separate two-ruler freeze contains 6,240 solves, 622,455 funded rows, 720
endpoint comparisons, 1,440 reversed-ID endpoint reruns, 288 separate GLOP
checks, and 26 objective-optimum basis diagnostics. Its dimensions are eight
windows by 26 months by five gammas by three coordinates by two rulers. It
loads no outcome column.

The separate credit-control freeze contains five score vectors for all 640,543
eligible rows, 160 residual recipes, 3,638,660 fit-audit rows, and 3,520
outcome-free geometry cells. It reproduces the CatBoost and numeric-logistic
score columns used in the detailed geometry audit exactly, and freezes
monotonic CatBoost plus both WOE/IV scorecards before any primary OOT outcome
join. No control enters a portfolio solve.

Each evaluator verifies its freeze identity and every artifact descriptor
before a keyed outcome join. Exact ID alignment is required; partial or
duplicated joins fail. The resulting evidence therefore separates allocation
construction from outcomes and prevents an outcome-dependent interpretation
from changing the frozen decision rule.

# Appendix B: Prediction and Binary Conformal Geometry

## B.1 Primary learner and four protocol-locked coverage controls

The primary score is a CatBoost classifier [@prokhorenkova2018catboost] with
seed 42, 29 numeric and nine
categorical origination-time features. A Platt map fitted on 2011 raw margins
[@platt2000] produces $p_i$. Five score strata, fixed from all status-independent 2011
scores, form the canonical Mondrian taxonomy. One-, two-, and ten-stratum
recipes are closed coverage diagnostics rather than a selection grid.
Only the four internal five-stratum cutpoints assign groups; the extreme bins
extend beyond the observed 2011 score range and therefore retain all later
valid scores.

Each learner needs a scalar score for residual construction; only the primary
CatBoost scalar also enters the portfolio LP. Platt scaling supplies that score
through a fixed logistic map fit on the separate 2011 block; its role is
architectural, not a claim of calibrator optimality.

A separate two-phase sensitivity freezes four monotone maps of the same
primary CatBoost base output on the same 14,077 availability-safe 2011 labels:
the active Platt logistic map, reused without refitting [@platt2000],
increasing isotonic regression with
clipped out-of-domain predictions [@zadrozny2002], beta calibration with the
`abm` parameterization [@kull2017], and
`VennAbers(setting="classification", precision=None)` [@vovk2014].
The scientific environment pins `betacal==1.1.0` and
`venn-abers==1.5.3`. If $p$ is the frozen Platt probability and $a,b$ are its
intercept and positive slope on the CatBoost raw margin, the common
uncalibrated CatBoost probability is reconstructed as

$$
q_{\mathrm{raw}}=
\operatorname{logit}^{-1}\!\left\{
\frac{\operatorname{logit}(p)-a}{b}
\right\}.
$$

No CatBoost model is refitted.

The four active Platt cutpoints are transformed through the same exact inverse.
They are not re-estimated as $q_{\mathrm{raw}}$ quantiles. This gives one common
five-stratum taxonomy with zero assignment changes, so method-specific ties in
isotonic or Venn--Abers predictions cannot change membership. Only residual
values may change; each window's row counts and finite-sample ranks remain
fixed. Phase A reuses Platt without refitting it, fits the other three maps, and
freezes all 160 method--window--stratum recipes before the target endpoint join. Because the
retrospective raw-file scan necessarily reads chunks containing status values
before filtering to the locked 2011 IDs, this is logical target-outcome nonuse,
not a physical lockbox. No primary-OOT outcome is retained or used in a map,
taxonomy, or recipe.

Venn--Abers returns the multiprobabilistic pair $(p_{i0},p_{i1})$. The declared
point score for this finite comparison is

$$
p_i^\prime=\frac{p_{i1}}{1-p_{i0}+p_{i1}},
$$

not the historical midpoint. The frozen artifact retains both pair components
and verifies $0\le p_{i0}\le p_i^\prime\le p_{i1}\le1$. The scalar does not
inherit the Venn multiprobability guarantee, is not a latent-PD interval, and
is not authorized as a portfolio endpoint. Phase B reports all four methods,
all eight windows, `ALL` plus all five common strata, and every unordered
method pair. It selects no map or result and runs no optimization. Neither this
sensitivity nor a calibrator name supplies temporal transport or
selected/funded-set coverage.

The executable primary specification uses 500 trees, depth 6, learning rate
0.04, `Balanced` automatic class weights, Bernoulli bootstrap with 0.80
subsampling, `has_time=true`, and a temporal validation tail comprising the
last 20% of PD-development months. These values and seed 42 are inherited from
the locked design rather than selected on downstream outcomes.

A numeric logistic regression provides the first coverage-only
control. It uses median imputation, standard scaling, class balancing, and its
own 2011 Platt map and fixed taxonomy. Three further controls use the same
temporal roles and all eligible rows:

- **Monotonic CatBoost.** Positive constraints apply to interest rate, DTI,
  loan-to-income and its square, installment burden, revolving utilization,
  revolving-balance-to-income, public records, recent inquiries, delinquency
  severity, and five adverse-history flags. Negative constraints apply to
  annual and log income, FICO, credit age, and delinquency recency. The inherited
  `recent_chargeoff` flag is constant in PD development and Platt calibration,
  so its declared positive constraint is inert in fitting.
- **Platform-signal WOE/IV.** Twenty-six fields include loan amount, interest,
  installment, income and burden ratios, revolving and bureau measures, grade,
  subgrade, home ownership, purpose, verification, interest bucket, and the
  interest-bucket-by-grade interaction.
- **Pricing-excluded application WOE/IV.** Nineteen fields retain loan amount, income, DTI,
  loan-to-income, revolving utilization and balances, FICO, credit age,
  employment length, account counts, public records, inquiries, delinquency,
  home ownership, purpose, and verification. Grade, subgrade, interest,
  installment, pricing buckets, and their interaction are excluded.

Each OptBinning process is fit on PD development only, with automatic
monotonic trend, two to eight bins, and a 5% minimum bin share
[@navaspalencia2020]. Each learner then receives its own 2011 Platt map and
taxonomy. None of the four controls enters the portfolio optimizer or is chosen
from OOT outcomes. They ask whether coverage transport is specific to model
class, unconstrained shape, or platform pricing; they are not a model-selection
contest.

| Learner | 2011 Platt-block AUC | 2011 Platt-block Brier |

The raw audit labels 30 origination fields as temporally eligible, whereas the
frozen model consumes engineered predictors rather than every eligible raw
column. Four eligible fields are deliberately absent. `initial_list_status`
and `policy_code` are constant in PD development. `acc_now_delinq` and
`delinq_amnt` have only a handful of nonzero early observations and are not
added beside the more stable delinquency history and severity features. This
is a prespecified representation choice, not a claim that the omitted fields
are unavailable or useless in another design.

The raw-feature contract records two exceptions to the 95% coverage threshold.
`mths_since_last_delinq` is structurally nullable: minimum fitting coverage is
0.336075 and primary OOT coverage is 0.528555; the frozen transformation maps
missing recency to 999. `pub_rec_bankruptcies` has minimum fitting coverage
0.921700 and complete primary OOT coverage; missing values map to no recorded
bankruptcy. Feature engineering emits observed-value indicators for audit, but
the active portfolio learner does not add them post hoc. Appendix B.7 reports
a dedicated feature-semantics-preserving encoding sensitivity for these two
fields. It does not cover every incomplete predictor, identify a missingness
mechanism, or select an encoding. In particular, `emp_length` availability
declines from 98.394% in PD development to 92.754% in primary OOT; CatBoost
retains its missing values natively, numeric logistic uses the development
median, and both WOE controls use their frozen missing-bin semantics. This is a
disclosed transport limitation rather than a new selected robustness family.

intercept/slope fits converge in 8--16 iterations. Among resolved primary OOT
outcomes, default prevalence is 0.156167, versus 0.104781 on the 2011 Platt

## B.3 Complete residual-window specification

<!-- claim:coverage.five_models_all_windows_below_nominal -->

For each learner, window, and fixed score stratum $g$, define residuals

$$
R_i=|Y_i-p_i|.
$$

At target miscoverage $\alpha=0.10$, the finite-sample split rank is

$$
k_g=\left\lceil(n_g+1)(1-\alpha)\right\rceil,
$$

and, when $k_g\le n_g$, $c_g=R_{(k_g)}$ is the $k_g$-th smallest residual under
ascending order. The standard $k_g=n_g+1$ convention is $+\infty$; the active
binary implementation stores the equivalent cap $c_g=1$, which includes both
candidate labels because $p_i,Y_i\in[0,1]$. The clipped interval is

$$
[\ell_i,u_i]=[\max(0,p_i-c_g),\min(1,p_i+c_g)].
$$

It predicts the observed binary outcome. It is not a confidence interval for
latent individual PD. The interval is not constructed as the convex hull of
its intersection with the binary outcome space and does not equal that hull in
general. The latter intersection is reported separately as empty, $\{0\}$,
$\{1\}$, or $\{0,1\}$.

|---|---:|---:|---:|
| W1 | 2012-01--2012-06 | 14,948 | 0.900388 |
| W2 | 2012-02--2012-07 | 16,674 | 0.900444 |
| W3 | 2012-03--2012-08 | 19,049 | 0.900362 |
| W4 | 2012-04--2012-09 | 21,767 | 0.900262 |

All eight windows are reported. The windows overlap, and their growing sample
sizes partly reflect platform growth. They are not independent temporal
replications.

## B.4 Candidate coverage with unresolved outcomes

Let $M_i=1\{Y_i\notin[\ell_i,u_i]\}$. Resolved coverage is computed on labeled
candidates. For each unresolved row, the evaluator computes the two attainable
values $M_i(0)$ and $M_i(1)$. Holding $M_i(Y_i)$ fixed for $i\in R$, the sharp
all-candidate coverage interval is

$$
\left[
1-n^{-1}\left\{\sum_{i\in R}M_i(Y_i)+\sum_{i\in U}\max_y M_i(y)\right\},
1-n^{-1}\left\{\sum_{i\in R}M_i(Y_i)+\sum_{i\in U}\min_y M_i(y)\right\}
\right].
$$

This matters
for empty, singleton, and $\{0,1\}$ sets: an unresolved outcome cannot be forced
to fail when both binary endpoints are covered, nor forced to succeed when the
set is empty.

### B.4.1 Joint-block combined-rank reference diagnostic

<!-- claim:coverage.joint_block_rank_reference_nominal_flags -->

The 40 sharp exclusions above do not themselves test an exchangeability
assumption. A separate locked lineage therefore compares the target miss count
with a one-sided upper-tail exact combined-rank law. Fix a learner, window, and
score stratum; let $n$ be the calibration count, $m$ the target count,
$r=\lceil(n+1)(1-\alpha)\rceil$, and $q=R_{(r)}$. Conditional on the frozen
taxonomy and realized stratum membership and counts $(n,m)$, if the $n+m$ residuals are
jointly continuous and exchangeable, the number of strict target misses obeys

$$
M=\sum_{j=1}^{m}1\{R_j>q\}
\sim \operatorname{BetaBinomial}(m,n+1-r,r).
$$

This is the finite-batch empirical-coverage law of
@marques2025universal, written for the complementary strict-miss count. The
adaptations used here are deterministic tie-safe domination and the worst-case
unresolved-label completion below, not a new Beta--Binomial law.

This is a joint block-exchangeability null for the calibration residuals and
all target residuals in the stratum. It is stronger than the
calibration-plus-one-target condition sufficient for ordinary split-conformal
marginal coverage; a flag may therefore reflect target--target dependence or
heterogeneity and does not directly refute one-point validity. The rank
statement does not require treating target rows as independent conditional
Bernoulli trials. With ties, attach independent
continuous auxiliary tie breakers to all residuals and order the resulting
pairs lexicographically. The paired count $M^*$ has the law above and every
deterministic strict miss is also a lexicographic miss, so $M\le M^*$
pointwise. The same upper tail is therefore conservative under arbitrary joint
exchangeability with ties; the auxiliary variables are a proof device and do
not change the fitted sets.

For unresolved outcomes, the sharp minimum miss count is

$$
M_{g,\min}=\sum_{i\in R_g}M_i(Y_i)+
\sum_{i\in U_g}\min\{M_i(0),M_i(1)\}.
$$

Because the beta--binomial upper tail decreases with the miss count, the
reported $p_g=\Pr(M\ge M_{g,\min})$ is the supremum p-value over all binary
completions. Within each learner--window cell the five stratum p-values form
$p_{\mathrm{cell}}=\min(1,5\min_g p_g)$; Holm is then applied over the 40
dependent cells. For an ex ante fixed family of valid p-values,
Bonferroni--Holm would control FWER at 0.05 without an independence assumption.
Here the family and an exploratory flag pattern were inspected before the
diagnostic was locked, so this is post-inspection reporting and the same cutoffs are nominal
within-table thresholds, not
post-selection or study-wide FWER control.

| Learner | Meets threshold | Does not meet | Windows meeting threshold |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| CatBoost | 8 | 0 | W1--W8 |
| Numeric logistic | 4 | 4 | W5--W8 |
| Monotonic CatBoost | 8 | 0 | W1--W8 |
| Platform-signal WOE | 6 | 2 | W3--W8 |
| Pricing-excluded application WOE | 5 | 3 | W4--W8 |
| **Total** | **31** | **9** | -- |

### B.4.2 Label-Mondrian retrospective sensitivity

<!-- claim:sensitivity.label_mondrian_complete_mixed -->
<!-- claim:sensitivity.label_mondrian_common_completion_gap -->

The active recipe is score-Mondrian but marginal over the label. A physically
separate outcome-free freeze also fits 400 class-specific thresholds,

$$
q_{gy}=R^{(gy)}_{(k_{gy})},\qquad
k_{gy}=\left\lceil(n_{gy}+1)(1-\alpha)\right\rceil,
$$

with $q_{gy}=+\infty$ if $k_{gy}=n_{gy}+1$. Evaluation constructs the discrete
set directly as

$$
S(p,g)=\{0:p\le q_{g0}\}\cup\{1:1-p\le q_{g1}\}.
$$

This is not generally the intersection of one symmetric interval with the
binary label space. Its standard class-conditional guarantee would require
exchangeability within every $(G,Y)$ cell, a distinct category-specific
target-period condition that this retrospective sensitivity does not establish.

40-cell label-Mondrian sensitivity. The sole lower-at-or-above cell is platform
WOE W8, with bound $[0.900074,0.907015]$; it is not promoted.

For any fixed aggregate or score-stratum reporting cell, suppress its non-label
indices. For a target class $y$, let $A_y$ and $B_y$ be covered and total
resolved class-$y$ counts, and let $U_y^0,U_y^1$ count unresolved rows that would be
missed or covered if assigned $y$. Every active cell has $B_y>0$, under which
its sharp ratio bounds are

$$
\left[\frac{A_y}{B_y+U_y^0},
\frac{A_y+U_y^1}{B_y+U_y^1}\right].
$$

For a generic cell with $B_y=0$, coverage is defined only for completions that
assign at least one row to class $y$; the extremization must exclude the empty
class rather than interpret $0/0$.

The two class endpoints may use different label completions. For each endpoint
of the class-0-minus-class-1 gap, every unresolved row is assigned only once and
that assignment is shared by both class ratios; the lower and upper gap
endpoints may themselves use different completions. Enumerating the possible
class-1 count gives the sharp extrema, whereas subtracting separately optimized
class intervals would not. All 40 aggregate gap bounds cross zero.

## B.5 Exact binary threshold geometry

<!-- claim:geometry.binary_threshold_phase_characterization -->

Because $s_i(Y_i)=p_i$ when $Y_i=0$ and $1-p_i$ when $Y_i=1$, the calibration
residuals of a stratum are the multiset sum of two mirror samples,
$R=\{\!\{p_i:Y_i=0\}\!\}\uplus\{\!\{1-p_i:Y_i=1\}\!\}$, and the fitted threshold
is exactly $c=R_{(k)}$ for $k$ from the split-conformal rank rule, provided
$p_i\in[0,1]$ and $k\le n$. With $A=\#\{Y_i=0,p_i<1/2\}$ and
$B=\#\{Y_i=1,p_i>1/2\}$,

$$
c<\tfrac12\iff A+B\ge k,
\qquad
n-k=\lfloor\alpha(n+1)\rfloor-1,
$$

the second identity being exact rather than approximate. Under the calibration
condition $\max_i p_i<1/2$ this reduces to $c<1/2$ if and only if the phase
margin $m=D-(n-k)$ is nonpositive, where $D$ is the calibration default count.
When both calibration classes are nonempty, under no interleaving, if $m\le0$
the threshold is the $k$-th smallest
nondefault score; if $m\ge1$ it is $1-p^1_{[m]}$, where $p^1_{[m]}$ is the
$m$-th largest default score. In particular, $m=0$ and $m=1$ yield the maximum
nondefault score and one minus the maximum default score in their respective
calibration blocks; they are not two states of a single fixed block.

Two conditions must be kept separate. With both calibration classes nonempty,
the weaker no-interleaving condition
$\max_{Y_i=0}p_i+\max_{Y_i=1}p_i<1$ determines only which mirror sample supplies
$c$. It does not place $c$ below one half: with $n=20$, $\alpha=0.10$, eighteen
nondefaults at $p=0.10$, one nondefault at $p=0.70$ and one default at $p=0.20$,
no-interleaving holds and $D=1\le n-k=1$, yet $c=0.70$. Every statement anchored
at one half therefore requires $\max_i p_i<1/2$ on the calibration block.

Statements about a target unit require their own support condition, because
neither calibration condition constrains target scores. Covering $Y=1$ requires
$p\ge1-c$, so every realized target default is missed exactly when none reaches
that boundary. For $c<1/2$, $S=\{1\}$ exactly when $p\ge1-c$; for $c\ge1/2$,
$S=\{1\}$ exactly when $p>c$. Hence, on a finite candidate panel,
$\max_i p_i<1-c$ is an outcome-free sufficient condition for both zero
positive-class coverage and no $\{1\}$ sets in the low regime, but it is not
necessary for the former. In the frozen taxonomy the open-ended top stratum has
target scores above one half for every learner, so these conditions must be
reported per stratum rather than assumed.

Changing calibration blocks can move the threshold and the resulting set
composition sharply. Section B.5.1 accounts for the coverage response separately
through target mass crossed by any two thresholds.

assignments, and gives each unresolved loan the same label under both thresholds.

For any binary outcome, interval miscoverage has the exact identity

$$
M_i=1\{Y_i=0,\ell_i>0\}+1\{Y_i=1,u_i<1\}.
$$

Endpoint saturation can therefore increase coverage without improving score
ranking, and a width reduction can increase missed rare positives.

### B.5.1 Exact coverage change between two thresholds

<!-- claim:theory.coverage_band_identity -->
<!-- claim:coverage.common_panel_adjacent_response -->

The same identity gives exact stratum coverage,
$\operatorname{Cov}_t=(1-\pi_t)\Pr_t(p\le c\mid Y=0)+\pi_t\Pr_t(p\ge 1-c\mid Y=1)$,
where the probabilities are evaluated directly with the displayed weak
inequalities. Equivalently, if the default-score CDF is used, the second term is
$1-F_{1,t}((1-c)^-)$. This holds with no separation condition and no regime.

For any fixed target distribution and $0\le c_L<c_H\le1$, evaluating the
coverage identity at both thresholds gives

$$
\operatorname{Cov}(c_H)-\operatorname{Cov}(c_L)
=(1-\pi_t)\Pr_t\!\left(c_L<p\le c_H\mid Y=0\right)
+\pi_t\Pr_t\!\left(1-c_H\le p<1-c_L\mid Y=1\right),
$$

which is exact and nonnegative. Endpoint inclusion is asymmetric: $p=c_H$ enters
the nondefault band, $p=1-c_H$ enters the default band, and the two lower-threshold
coverage endpoints do not. The formula says the response is determined by target
mass in the crossed bands, not by $|c_H-c_L|$. It does not imply continuity: with
$c_L=.2$, $c_H=.7$, and target points $(Y,p)=(0,.4),(1,.5)$, coverage changes from
zero to one despite varying scores.

For an ordered change from a fitted threshold $c_f$ to $c_t$, including a
decrease, define the two possible label-specific changes

$$
d_i(0)=1\{p_i\le c_t\}-1\{p_i\le c_f\},\qquad
d_i(1)=1\{p_i\ge 1-c_t\}-1\{p_i\ge 1-c_f\}.
$$

If $R$ and $U$ index resolved and unresolved candidates, respectively, the
sharp all-candidate finite-archive bounds are

$$
\left[
\frac{\sum_{i\in R}d_i(Y_i)+\sum_{i\in U}\min\{d_i(0),d_i(1)\}}{N},
\frac{\sum_{i\in R}d_i(Y_i)+\sum_{i\in U}\max\{d_i(0),d_i(1)\}}{N}
\right].
$$

Every unresolved label is assigned once and shared between the from and to
coverage terms. Consequently the exact identification width is
$N^{-1}\sum_{i\in U}|d_i(1)-d_i(0)|$. For $c_t>c_f$, the resolved numerator is
the number of resolved nondefaults in $c_f<p\le c_t$ plus the number of
resolved defaults in $1-c_t\le p<1-c_f$; for $c_t<c_f$, it is the negative of
the corresponding counts with the interval endpoints reversed. These signed
crossed-band identities preserve the asymmetric endpoint conventions above.

We applied this calculation to the fixed 376,890-candidate primary panel for
every adjacent calibration-window pair, learner, and frozen five-group score
stratum: $7\times5\times5=175$ stratum transitions. Because each binary
coverage indicator is monotone in $c$, every stratum response has the sign of
$c_t-c_f$ unless no candidate changes membership. Accordingly, the 122
negative, 48 positive, and 5 exact $[0,0]$ responses are an exhaustive
consistency census rather than a substantive sign discovery; none strictly
straddles or merely touches zero. What the replay identifies is the crossed
class mass, response magnitude, and sharp width. Because the five stratum
thresholds can move in different directions, the learner aggregate need not
inherit one threshold sign. Summing integer numerators across mutually exclusive
strata before division gives 35 learner-transition responses: 31 negative, none
containing zero, and 4 positive. The full rows are machine-readable Tables
S6J--S6K; the complete fixed-order heatmap appears in Supplemental Figure S1
below.
Across the 175 cellwise bounds, the identification-width median is 0.0185
percentage points, the 90th percentile is 0.1063 points, and the maximum is
0.2346 points. These archive-inspected summaries are descriptive, not
predeclared uncertainty targets.

$[-0.003947,-0.003669]$. Among the unresolved loans, 31 lie in the union of the

symmetric-difference loan contributes either $-1$ or 0; this gives the

$22/79{,}047=0.000278$. Band overlap does not double-count a resolved loan:
its realized label selects exactly one of $d_i(0)$ or $d_i(1)$.
For this one cell, the two response endpoints happen numerically to equal the
same-side differences of the Table S7 marginal bounds (W8 lower minus W7 lower,
and W8 upper minus W7 upper). That coincidence follows from the observed
unresolved transition pattern: 22 full-to-singleton, 9 full-to-empty, and no
singleton-to-empty transitions. It does not authorize subtraction of separately
extremized intervals in another cell.

W7 and W8 are overlapping but distinct calibration blocks. Their thresholds
must not be described as a unit flip of one fixed block or through one shared
pair of calibration maxima. This replay directly identifies what changed in
coverage on the fixed archive, but not why either threshold moved, why target
scores occupied the crossed bands, or whether the response transports.
Threshold distance alone supplies no coverage bound. The census is
retrospective and descriptive; it is not preregistered confirmation, a slope or
continuity estimate, a learner/window selection exercise, a causal mechanism,
or a restoration of funded-set conformal validity.
Each interval is sharp for its cell separately. Because adjacent contrasts
overlap, no claim is made that all 350 displayed endpoints are jointly
attainable under one global vector of unresolved-label completions.

### B.5.2 Sharp outcome-free bounds for a fixed allocation

<!-- claim:theory.outcome_free_binary_set_bounds -->

Let $S_i\subseteq\{0,1\}$ be the prediction set for loan $i$, let $a_i\ge0$
be fixed allocation weights, and let $B_a=\sum_i a_i>0$. For every binary
outcome vector $Y$,

$$
\frac{\sum_i a_i\mathbf 1\{S_i=\varnothing\}}{B_a}
\le
\frac{\sum_i a_i\mathbf 1\{Y_i\notin S_i\}}{B_a}
\le
1-\frac{\sum_i a_i\mathbf 1\{S_i=\{0,1\}\}}{B_a}.
$$

The bounds are sharp without outcome restrictions. An empty set misses both
possible labels, a full set covers both, and for every singleton one can choose
the contained label to attain the lower endpoint or the excluded label to
attain the upper endpoint. These choices are loan-wise, so zero allocation and
ties cause no exception.

For an interval embedding $[\ell_i,u_i]$, the lower endpoint being positive is
not itself a funded miss: $[0.6,1]$ covers $Y_i=1$. Similarly,
$\sum_i a_i\mathbf 1\{u_i=1\}/B_a$ is the share of total allocated capital
whose induced set can cover label one. It is neither positive-class coverage
nor a conformal guarantee after allocation. Thus the result is fixed-allocation
binary-set algebra; it supplies no universal optimizer direction and no
selected-set conformal claim.

### B.5.3 Set-equivalent continuous embeddings

<!-- claim:theory.binary_set_embedding_nonidentification -->

For $0\le\ell\le u\le1$, membership of zero depends only on $\ell=0$ and
membership of one only on $u=1$. Hence

$$
\begin{aligned}
S=\varnothing&\iff \ell>0,\ u<1,&
S=\{0\}&\iff \ell=0,\ u<1,\\
S=\{1\}&\iff \ell>0,\ u=1,&
S=\{0,1\}&\iff \ell=0,\ u=1.
\end{aligned}
$$

This proves Lemma 1 and shows exactly what the binary set identifies. In the
active absolute-residual embedding, $\ell\le p\le u$. If $1\notin S$, then
$p\le u<1$ and $u^{(\theta)}=(1-\theta)u+\theta p$ remains in $[p,u]$ for
every $\theta\in[0,1]$; if $1\in S$, keep $u^{(\theta)}=1$. Thus
$[\ell,u^{(\theta)}]\cap\{0,1\}=S$ exactly and all candidate coverage
indicators are invariant, including at the endpoints. For any $\gamma>0$,
however, the downstream coefficient changes by $\gamma\theta(p-u)$ whenever
$1\notin S$ and $u>p$. Whether the LP allocation or its outcome bounds change
is empirical and must be reported over a complete outcome-free-frozen
sensitivity; the algebra alone neither proves an allocation change nor selects
a $\theta$. Appendix E.4.3 reports that separate empirical census.

The full compatible fibre is larger than the contraction used by that census.
If every interval is constrained to contain its center $p_i$ and
$0<\gamma\le1$, then

$$
q_i\in
\begin{cases}
\{p_i+\gamma(1-p_i)\},&1\in S_i,\\
[p_i,p_i+\gamma(1-p_i)),&1\notin S_i.
\end{cases}
$$

At $\gamma=0$, $q_i=p_i$. If $I=\{i:1\notin S_i\}$, the linear span of
all compatible coefficient differences is
$\operatorname{span}\{e_i:i\in I\}$. Consequently the continuous functional
is identified on the feasible-difference space $D$ for every compatible
embedding exactly when this coordinate subspace lies in $D^\perp$; otherwise
the global invariance theorem need not apply. This statement permits a decision
change but does not require one at a fixed cell.

There is also a sharp caution for naive robustification. Under rectangular
loan-wise ambiguity and $a_i\ge0$,

$$
\sup_{q\text{ compatible}}q^\top a
=\sum_i a_i\{p_i+\gamma(1-p_i)\}.
$$

For $1\notin S_i$ the endpoint is generally a supremum over an open fibre, not
an attained maximum. At $\gamma=1$ the robust coefficient is therefore one for
every loan. A full-budget cap $q^\top a\le\tau B$ is infeasible when $\tau<1$;
if cash is permitted through $\sum_i a_i\le B$, the same robust constraint
reduces to $\sum_i a_i\le\tau B$ and ceases to distinguish loans (and is
redundant at $\tau=1$). Cross-loan restrictions or an exogenous endpoint bound
below one would define a different uncertainty model. This fibre-specific
corollary is not a general theorem that nonidentified scores must change an
optimizer.

For the active score
$q_i^{(\theta)}=(1-\gamma)p_i+\gamma u_i^{(\theta)}$, the contraction has the
more explicit form

$$
q_i^{(\theta)}-q_i^{(0)}
=-\gamma\theta c_{g(i)}\mathbf1\{1\notin S_i\}.
$$

This preserves the loan-wise miss map
$m_i(y)=\mathbf1\{y\notin S_i\}$ but need not be positive-affine on the
allocation space. Consequently, for any two fully invested allocations
$a^\theta,a^0$ and every common binary outcome completion $Y$,

$$
\operatorname{MC}_{\theta}(Y)-\operatorname{MC}_{0}(Y)
=B^{-1}(a^\theta-a^0)^\top m(Y).
$$

There is no direct prediction-set term: any funded-miscoverage change comes
from reweighting an unchanged miss map. The identity supplies neither a
universal sign nor funded-set conformal validity.

one, observed zeros to zero, and only unavailable values become null in the
native arm. The intervention is limited to `mths_since_last_delinq` and
`pub_rec_bankruptcies`; it is not a general missingness stress over all model
features, including `emp_length`. Thus the comparison changes the declared

0.875261, respectively. The substantially lower later-origin lower bounds
reflect its larger unresolved fraction; they should not be read as a more
severe resolved-case coverage failure. The historical 376,890-row, 15-month
panel is explicitly rejected from this comparison. No origin is selected, and
two origins cannot establish temporal invariance or prospective performance.

# Appendix C: Portfolio and Comparator Protocol

## C.1 Model-implied plug-in objective and status-indexed endpoint

For candidate $i$ with listed amount $L_i$, contractual annual rate $r_i$, point score
$p_i$, and LGD $\lambda=0.45$, the optimizer uses

$$
v_i=(1-p_i)r_i-p_i\lambda.
$$

The status-indexed standardized payoff proxy uses the algebraically coherent endpoint

$$
z_i(Y_i)=(1-Y_i)r_i-Y_i\lambda.
$$

Thus $v_i$ is the model-implied expectation of $z_i$ if $p_i$ were the true
conditional event probability. The audit does not assert that condition. The
endpoint is not investor return, IRR, NPV, welfare, or a cash-flow model; it
omits amortization, prepayment timing, recovery timing, fees, discounting, and
capital costs.

## C.2 Monthly linear program

For score $s_i$ and cap $\tau$, each monthly policy solves

$$
\begin{aligned}
\max_a\quad & \sum_i a_i v_i \\
\text{s.t.}\quad
& \sum_i a_i=B,\\
& 0\le a_i\le L_i,\\
& \sum_i a_i s_i\le \tau B,\\
& \sum_{i:\operatorname{purpose}_i=h}a_i\le0.25B
  \quad\text{for each purpose }h,
\end{aligned}
$$

with $B=\$1{,}000{,}000$. The point policy uses $s_i=p_i$. The guardrail uses

$$
q_i(\gamma)=(1-\gamma)p_i+\gamma u_i.
$$

The complete score path is
$\gamma\in\{0,0.25,0.50,0.75,1\}$. The frozen empirical contrast is
$\gamma=1$ minus $\gamma=0$; the three interior gamma values diagnose the path
and cannot be selected as winners.

## C.3 Two common-frontier rulers

Let $\mathcal A_t$ contain the nonrisk constraints above, let
$s(\gamma)=q(\gamma)$, and define

$$
m_{\gamma t}=B^{-1}\min_{a\in\mathcal A_t}s(\gamma)^\top a,
\quad z_t^*=\max_{a\in\mathcal A_t}v^\top a,
\quad o_{\gamma t}=B^{-1}s(\gamma)^\top a_t^*.
$$

For the primary **objective-matched ruler**, define the objective-efficient
point on the minimum-score face by

$$
z^{\min}_{\gamma t}
=\max\{v^\top a:a\in\mathcal A_t,\ s(\gamma)^\top a=B m_{\gamma t}\},
$$

with the registered solver tolerances, and let
$z_t^L=\max_\gamma z^{\min}_{\gamma t}$. At
$\rho\in\{.25,.50,.75\}$ every score minimizes funded score subject to the
same objective floor

$$
v^\top a\ge z_t^L+\rho(z_t^*-z_t^L).
$$

This matches model-implied objective sacrifice, not true expected return. For
the secondary **normalized-score ruler**, define

$$
c_{\gamma t}(\eta)=m_{\gamma t}
 +\eta(o_{\gamma t}-m_{\gamma t}),\qquad
\eta\in\{.25,.50,.75\},
$$

and maximize the plug-in objective under
$s(\gamma)^\top a\le Bc_{\gamma t}(\eta)$. This coordinate is invariant to
positive affine score units, but it does not match objective sacrifice,
default risk, or shadow price. Coordinate one reaches the common verified
plug-in objective value for every gamma and is therefore a structural null only
for that objective-value contrast. Allocation and status-indexed endpoint
contrasts also require a unique common optimizer or reuse of the same optimizer
by definition. The evaluated three-coordinate interior grid is finite; it is
not a continuous two-ruler frontier.

## C.4 Supporting named comparators and registered support

The earlier fixed-cap grid supplies supporting comparator diagnostics:

| Policy | $\tau$ | $\gamma$ | Policy | $\tau$ | $\gamma$ | Policy | $\tau$ | $\gamma$ |
|---|---:|---:|---|---:|---:|---|---:|---:|
| P1 | 0.15 | 0.25 | P4 | 0.17 | 0.25 | P7 | 0.19 | 0.25 |
| P2 | 0.15 | 0.50 | P5 | 0.17 | 0.50 | P8 | 0.19 | 0.50 |
| P3 | 0.15 | 0.75 | P6 | 0.17 | 0.75 | P9 | 0.19 | 0.75 |

**Table S8.** Supporting fixed-cap grid. It is not a closed policy family and no policy is selected or promoted.

The score and its cap jointly define a feasible decision problem. The audit
therefore declares four point-score comparison objects.

**C0: same numeric cap.** The point policy copies the guardrail's $\tau$. Since
$q_i\ge p_i$, this is a positive control for mechanical feasible-set nesting,
not a neutral baseline.

**C1: development mean.** For each window-policy pair, the point cap is the
capital-weighted mean of the guardrail allocation's point-score moments over
the eleven common February--December 2013 development menus.

**C2: contemporaneous funded-moment match.** After a guardrail allocation
$a^q$ is frozen on an OOT menu, the point cap is

$$
\tau^{C2}=\frac{\sum_i a_i^q p_i}{B}.
$$

This is outcome-free, menu-adaptive, and executable at decision time. Its cap is
nevertheless endogenous to the guardrail allocation it evaluates, so C2 is a
two-solve decomposition comparator. It is not a promoted operating policy, an
independently specified baseline, or a matched feasible-set counterfactual.

**Registered cap audit.** Each window-policy pair declares the closed
minimum--maximum interval of its eleven monthly development point-score moments;
their global hull is $[0.055573,0.099997]$. A secondary registered audit range is
$[0.05,0.12]$. Named range endpoints and HiGHS solver-reported range-record
values produce 3,067 distinct registered point caps. The intervals and
registered values are fixed without outcomes; the finite values are not an
exhaustive continuous path.

## C.5 Allocation granularity diagnostic

The LP permits fractional dollar exposure. To diagnose whether that relaxation
drives the reported rates, an outcome-free transformation floors each positive
baseline exposure to the nearest USD 25 lot and leaves the monthly residual as
cash. It does not redistribute cash, resolve a mixed-integer program, change a
ruler, or select a track. Both rounded and continuous outcomes are normalized
by the same committed capital, so cash remains visible rather than silently
renormalizing the rounded portfolio upward.

# Appendix D: Exact Statements and Proofs

## D.1 Combined-rank miss law and tie-safe domination

The tie-free distribution below is the exact finite-batch empirical-coverage
law of @marques2025universal, written for the complementary strict-miss count.
We reproduce the combined-rank derivation to make the parameter order explicit
and then establish the two adaptations used here: deterministic tie-safe
domination and worst-case unresolved-label completion.

Fix one pre-existing score stratum and condition on the frozen taxonomy and its
realized membership and counts $(n,m)$. Assume $r\le n$, as in every evaluated
stratum. If $r=n+1$, the standard fitted threshold is $+\infty$ and the
strict-miss count is degenerate at zero; the active binary implementation's
stored cap $1$ is equivalent for residuals in $[0,1]$. Under joint
exchangeability and continuity,
the calibration indices occupy a uniformly distributed $n$-subset of the
$n+m$ combined residual ranks. Let $r$ be the fitted calibration order and let
$M$ count target ranks above the $r$-th calibration rank. The uniform-rank
count gives

$$
\Pr(M=j)=\binom mj
\frac{\mathrm B(j+n+1-r,m-j+r)}{\mathrm B(n+1-r,r)},
\qquad j=0,\ldots,m,
$$

which is the beta--binomial distribution with parameters
$(m,n+1-r,r)$. Equivalently, the number of target ranks occurring after the
$r$-th calibration rank has the same beta--binomial urn count. This argument
uses exchangeability of the combined ranks; an i.i.d. representation is not
needed. It is nevertheless a joint-block assumption on all $m$ targets, not
merely the calibration-plus-one-target condition used for a pointwise marginal
split-conformal guarantee.

When residuals tie, augment every calibration and target residual with an
independent continuous tie breaker and order pairs lexicographically. Joint
exchangeability is preserved and the pair ranks are almost surely distinct, so
their exceedance count $M^*$ obeys the displayed law. The scalar value of the
$r$-th calibration pair remains the fitted scalar threshold $q$. If $R_j>q$,
then $(R_j,U_j)$ necessarily exceeds that pair; if $R_j=q$, it may or may not.
Consequently the deterministic strict-miss count satisfies $M_{\rm det}\le
M^*$ for every realization. Hence

$$
\Pr(M_{\rm det}\ge t)\le \Pr(M^*\ge t),
$$

so the beta--binomial upper tail is exact in the continuous case and
conservative with arbitrary ties. Finally, $M_{g,\min}$ is attained by choosing
the less adverse binary endpoint independently for each unresolved loan. Since
the upper tail is nonincreasing in its threshold, its p-value is the supremum
over all unrestricted binary completions. For an ex ante fixed family,
Bonferroni within each five-stratum cell followed by Holm over 40 cells controls
the declared familywise level without an independence assumption. Because this
family and an exploratory flag pattern were inspected before locking, the
reported cutoffs have no post-selection FWER guarantee.

## D.2 Feasible-difference score equivalence and cap consequences

<!-- claim:theory.feasible_difference_score_order_equivalence -->

Let $\mathcal A\subset\mathbb R^n$ be the fixed nonempty convex allocation set
before adding a score constraint and define

$$
D=\operatorname{span}(\mathcal A-\mathcal A).
$$

Call scores $s,t$ *order-equivalent on $\mathcal A$* when
$s^\top a\le s^\top b$ if and only if $t^\top a\le t^\top b$ for every
$a,b\in\mathcal A$.

**Theorem.** The scores are order-equivalent on $\mathcal A$ if and only if
there are $\kappa>0$ and $h\in D^\perp$ such that

$$
t=\kappa s+h.
$$

Equivalently, for any fixed $a_0\in\mathcal A$, there is a constant
$\delta=t^\top a_0-\kappa s^\top a_0$ such that
$t^\top a=\kappa s^\top a+\delta$ for every $a\in\mathcal A$.

The forward direction is immediate because
$h^\top(a-b)=0$ on $\mathcal A$. For the converse, choose $a_0$ in the
relative interior of $\mathcal A$. A sufficiently small displacement from
$a_0$ in either direction of any $d\in D$ remains in $\mathcal A$. Equality
of weak orders therefore forces the restrictions of
$d\mapsto s^\top d$ and $d\mapsto t^\top d$ to have the same kernel and sign
on $D$. If the first functional vanishes on $D$, so does the second; taking
any $\kappa>0$, for example $\kappa=1$, then gives
$t-\kappa s\in D^\perp$. Otherwise choose $d_0\in D$ with
$s^\top d_0=1$. For every $d\in D$,
$d-(s^\top d)d_0$ is in the common kernel, so

$$
t^\top d=(t^\top d_0)s^\top d.
$$

The common sign gives $\kappa=t^\top d_0>0$, and hence
$t-\kappa s\in D^\perp$.

If the affine hull is exactly the full-budget hyperplane
$\mathbf1^\top a=B$, then $D=\mathbf1^\perp$ and
$t=\kappa s+b\mathbf1$. More generally, if
$\operatorname{aff}(\mathcal A)=\{a:Ea=d\}$, then
$D^\perp=\operatorname{range}(E^\top)$. Only equalities defining the complete
affine hull belong in this global normal term; a constraint active at one
solution provides at most a local condition.

For any total-score cap $K_s$, let $K_t=\kappa K_s+\delta$. The theorem gives

$$
\mathcal A\cap\{a:s^\top a\le K_s\}
=
\mathcal A\cap\{a:t^\top a\le K_t\}.
$$

With a common full budget $B$, the corresponding per-dollar caps
$\tau_s=K_s/B$ and $\tau_t=K_t/B$ satisfy
$\tau_t=\kappa\tau_s+\delta/B$. In the full-budget special case
$t=\kappa s+b\mathbf1$, this becomes $\tau_t=\kappa\tau_s+b$ because
$\delta=bB$.

The additive-offset conclusion uses the full-budget equality. If cash is added
as a zero-score decision coordinate and loan investment may be strictly below
$B$, shifting only the loan scores by $b$ adds $b\sum_i a_i$, not one common
constant, and need not preserve portfolio order unless $b=0$ (or cash receives
the same affine shift). The floor-with-cash diagnostic must therefore not borrow
the full-budget translation mechanically.

Thus translated caps preserve the feasible set. For the optimizer corollaries,
assume that the invoked feasible sets are nonempty and the stated optima are
attained, as they are on the bounded CRPTO allocation polytope. For any common
plug-in objective floor $z$, the restrictions of the two scores to
$\mathcal A_z=\mathcal A\cap\{a:v^\top a\ge z\}$ differ only by the same positive
affine transformation, and therefore

$$
\arg\min_{a\in\mathcal A_z}s^\top a
=
\arg\min_{a\in\mathcal A_z}t^\top a.
$$

Section D.3 gives the normalized-coordinate corollary. Copying the same
numerical cap is not the required translation unless both scale and offset
make it so.

The theorem concerns portfolio functionals, not only loan rankings. On the
unit simplex, $s=(0,.6,1)$ and $t=s^2=(0,.36,1)$ rank all three loans in the
same order, but they reverse the portfolio order between $e_2$ and
$.5(e_1+e_3)$. Binary-set preservation is weaker still. Take
$p=(.3,.1,.8)$ and thresholds $c=(.3,.6,.3)$. The original intervals are
$[0,.6]$, $[0,.7]$, and $[.5,1]$; full contraction gives $[0,.3]$,
$[0,.1]$, and $[.5,1]$. Both constructions induce
$\{0\},\{0\},\{1\}$, while at $\gamma=1$ their score vectors are

$$
q^{(0)}=(.6,.7,1),\qquad
q^{(1)}=(.3,.1,1).
$$

With plug-in objective $v=(0,0,1)$, the normalized ruler at $\eta=.5$ chooses
$(.5,0,.5)$ under $q^{(0)}$ and $(0,.5,.5)$ under $q^{(1)}$. At the common
objective floor $v^\top a\ge.25$, the objective-matched score minima are
$(.75,0,.25)$ and $(0,.75,.25)$. The attained plug-in objective is unchanged
in the latter pair, but the allocation is not.

Failure of the global condition permits rather than requires a change at one
fixed cell. For arbitrary fixed total-score caps $K_s,K_t$, let
$F_s=\mathcal A\cap\{a:s^\top a\le K_s\}$ and
$F_t=\mathcal A\cap\{a:t^\top a\le K_t\}$. Invariance for every linear
objective is equivalent to $F_s=F_t$. For one declared objective $v$, only
equality of its exposed optimal faces is required. A point
$a^\star\in F_s\cap F_t$ is optimal for both problems when $v$ belongs to both
relevant normal cones. One common numerical solver output therefore proves
neither equality of faces nor optimizer uniqueness.

More precisely, use the maximization convention

$$
N_F(a)=\{w:w^\top(x-a)\le0\ \text{for every }x\in F\}.
$$

For nonempty compact polytopes $F_s,F_t$, a point $a^\star$ is optimal for the
same objective $v$ on both if and only if

$$
a^\star\in F_s\cap F_t,
\qquad
v\in N_{F_s}(a^\star)\cap N_{F_t}(a^\star).
$$

If $a^\star$ is a vertex of both polytopes and $v$ lies in the relative
interior of both normal cones, it is the unique optimizer of both. Equality of
the complete exposed optimal face instead requires one common face $G$ and
$v\in\operatorname{ri}N_{F_s}(G)\cap\operatorname{ri}N_{F_t}(G)$. The
distinction is observable even in two dimensions: for
$F_s=[0,1]^2$, $F_t=\operatorname{conv}\{(0,0),(1,0),(0,1)\}$, and $v=(1,0)$,
a solver may return $(1,0)$ for both, although the first optimum is the full
edge $\{1\}\times[0,1]$ and the second is unique. Common output certifies at
most co-optimality unless the faces and cone interiors are audited.

As a related but different use of the same geometry, Wei and Zhang characterize
co-optimal linear objectives over one common feasible set by
common-normal-cone membership [@wei2024adjustability]. Their local
co-optimality condition can explain one shared optimum; CRPTO instead fixes the
objective while its score constraint can change the feasible set, and the
result is not the global weak-order equivalence over every feasible allocation
characterized above.

Finally, because $u_i\ge p_i$ and $\gamma\in[0,1]$, $q_i\ge p_i$. At the same
numerical cap, every guardrail-feasible allocation is point-feasible. The
point optimum therefore weakly dominates in the shared plug-in objective.
Neither nesting nor the equivalence theorem orders status-indexed outcomes.

## D.3 Positive-affine invariance of normalized coordinates

Under the theorem in D.2, let the total portfolio score satisfy
$t^\top a=\kappa s^\top a+\delta$ on $\mathcal A$. The minimum total score and
the score of a common plug-in optimum transform as
$M_t=\kappa M_s+\delta$ and $O_t=\kappa O_s+\delta$. Hence

$$
K_t(\eta)
=M_t+\eta(O_t-M_t)
=\kappa K_s(\eta)+\delta.
$$

Therefore $t^\top a\le K_t(\eta)$ if and only if
$s^\top a\le K_s(\eta)$. With a full budget and
$t=\kappa s+b\mathbf1$, division by $B$ recovers the paper's per-dollar
formula $c_t(\eta)=\kappa c_s(\eta)+b$. The normalized ruler defines the same
feasible set and optimizer correspondence under a common anchor. The result
does not extend to an unverified non-affine point-versus-upper score map, to a
different allocation affine hull, or to a different anchor; it also does not
equalize plug-in opportunity cost across arbitrary scores.

## D.4 C2 plug-in objective dominance

Let $a^q$ be a full-budget guardrail allocation and set
$c=p^\top a^q/B$. Then $p^\top a^q=cB$, so $a^q$ is feasible for the point LP
with cap $c$. Every nonrisk constraint and the plug-in objective are unchanged.
Consequently,

$$
V_p^*(c)\ge v^\top a^q.
$$

Across all 1,080 C2 cells, the maximum absolute funded-moment residual is
$8.33\times10^{-17}$. The minimum point-minus-guardrail plug-in objective is
$-1.46\times10^{-10}$ dollars, numerical zero within solver tolerance. This
reconciles the theorem; it does not establish status-indexed payoff dominance.

## D.5 Sharp common-outcome bounds

<!-- claim:theory.sharp_common_outcome_bounds -->

For fixed exposure weights $w_i$ and an additive binary endpoint
$f_i(Y_i)$, each unresolved outcome may be zero or one. The fixed-policy lower
and upper bounds are

$$
\sum_{i\in R}w_i f_i(Y_i)+
\sum_{i\in U}\min_{y\in\{0,1\}}w_i f_i(y),
\qquad
\sum_{i\in R}w_i f_i(Y_i)+
\sum_{i\in U}\max_{y\in\{0,1\}}w_i f_i(y).
$$

Here and throughout, the displayed bracket is the sharp endpoint hull: each
endpoint is attainable under one admissible joint binary completion, but the
finite identified set need not fill every interior value. Sharpness is
cellwise unless joint attainability across reported cells is stated.

For candidate coverage, $f_i=1-M_i$ gives the equivalent and operationally
clear form, with observed miss indicators fixed for $i\in R$ and only
unresolved labels extremized:

$$
C_L=1-\frac{1}{n}\left\{\sum_{i\in R}M_i(Y_i)+
\sum_{i\in U}\max_{y\in\{0,1\}}M_i(y)\right\},
\qquad
C_U=1-\frac{1}{n}\left\{\sum_{i\in R}M_i(Y_i)+
\sum_{i\in U}\min_{y\in\{0,1\}}M_i(y)\right\}.
$$

These are not obtained by adding or subtracting the unresolved fraction from
resolved coverage; the attainable miss values depend on each prediction set.

For a paired contrast, one common unresolved $Y_i$ is optimized over the union
of loans funded by either policy. This avoids the invalid operation of assigning
different outcomes to the same unresolved loan under two policies. The bounds
are sharp for the finite archive under unrestricted binary completion. They are
not sampling confidence intervals.

Class-specific coverage is a ratio rather than an additive endpoint. Fix one
aggregate or score-stratum reporting cell and suppress its non-label indices.
Every active reported cell has $B_0>0$ and $B_1>0$; for a generic cell, any
class ratio is defined only for completions with a positive class denominator.
For class $y$, write $z_i=1$ when unresolved loan $i$ is assigned that class and
$c_i=C_i(y)$. Then

$$
C_y(z)=\frac{A_y+\sum_i z_i c_i}{B_y+\sum_i z_i}.
$$

Adding a missed row cannot increase this ratio and adding a covered row cannot
decrease it. Therefore the sharp lower endpoint assigns all and only the
$U_y^0$ missed rows to class $y$, while the upper endpoint assigns all and only
the $U_y^1$ covered rows, giving the bounds in Section B.4.2.

Those two extrema need not use the same completion. For the gap $C_0-C_1$,
let $z_i=1$ instead denote assignment to class 1 and fix
$m=\sum_i z_i$. Both denominators are then fixed. The gap is a constant plus
a sum of $m$ loan-wise weights,

$$
\sum_i z_i\left\{-\frac{C_i(0)}{B_0+|U|-m}
-\frac{C_i(1)}{B_1+m}\right\}.
$$

Selecting the $m$ smallest weights minimizes the gap and selecting the $m$
largest maximizes it. The exact enumeration is over

$$
\mathcal M=\{m\in\{0,\ldots,|U|\}:B_1+m>0,\ B_0+|U|-m>0\}.
$$

Because both resolved classes are nonempty in every active reporting cell,
$\mathcal M=\{0,\ldots,|U|\}$ there. The restricted formulation is the valid
generic statement and uses
one common label for every unresolved loan. This proves the reported sharp gap
bounds; subtracting two separately optimized class intervals would generally
be only an outer bound.

<!-- claim:theory.binary_identification_width -->

For any additive paired contrast with unresolved contribution $d_i(Y_i)$,
separability gives the exact width

$$
U-L=\sum_{i\in U}|d_i(1)-d_i(0)|.
$$

Let $\delta_i=a_i^A-a_i^B$. For declared positive capital normalizers
$N_A,N_B$, define $\delta_i^w=a_i^A/N_A-a_i^B/N_B$. The reported widths are
therefore

$$
\begin{aligned}
W_{\mathrm{payoff}}&=\sum_{i\in U}|\delta_i|(r_i+\lambda),\\
W_{\mathrm{payoff\ rate}}&=\sum_{i\in U}|\delta_i^w|(r_i+\lambda),\\
W_{\mathrm{default}}&=\sum_{i\in U}|\delta_i^w|,\\
W_{\mathrm{miss}}&=\sum_{i\in U}|\delta_i^w|\,|m_i(1)-m_i(0)|.
\end{aligned}
$$

The last factorization assumes both policies use the same frozen prediction-set
map $m_i(y)$, as they do in the active comparisons. With policy-specific maps,
the general width identity still holds for
$d_i(y)=a_i^A m_i^A(y)/N_A-a_i^B m_i^B(y)/N_B$, but the displayed simplification
does not follow.

The active fully invested policies set $N_A=N_B=B$. The floor-with-cash
diagnostic retains the same committed-capital denominator $B$ so that cash is
not removed by renormalization. Resolved loans contribute zero width.
Unresolved loans funded identically by both policies also contribute zero; for
miscoverage, so do unresolved loans whose prediction set gives the same miss
indicator at both binary outcomes.
Identification loss is consequently governed by exposure disagreement and
binary set geometry, not by the unresolved count alone.

### D.5.1 Directional residual-distribution frontier

<!-- claim:theory.sharp_directional_residual_frontier -->

Fix a calibration empirical CDF $F^{\mathrm{cal}}$. For unresolved target row
$i$, binary completion permits residual $p_i$ or $1-p_i$. At every threshold
$t$,

$$
1\{\min(p_i,1-p_i)\le t\}\ge
1\{|Y_i-p_i|\le t\}\ge
1\{\max(p_i,1-p_i)\le t\}.
$$

Summing this inequality with the resolved-row indicators proves the pointwise
CDF sandwich $F^-\ge F_Y\ge F^+$. The functional
$\sup_t(F^{\mathrm{cal}}-F)$ is antitone in $F$, whereas
$\sup_t(F-F^{\mathrm{cal}})$ is monotone. Substituting the two attainable CDF
envelopes therefore gives all four extrema in
the main-text directional frontier. Because empirical CDF differences change only
at observed residuals, evaluating the union of calibration and target residual
values is exact and the smallest maximizing value supplies a finite witness.
No stochastic null or asymptotic KS reference is used.

### D.5.2 Selected-count, invested-dollar, and fixed-capital estimands

<!-- claim:theory.selection_weight_covariance_identity -->

On any fixed nonempty panel, allow $a_i\ge0$, require $A=\sum_i a_i>0$, use
divisor $N$ for empirical moments, and write
$\bar a=A/N$ and $\bar m=N^{-1}\sum_i m_i$. Direct expansion gives

$$
\frac{\operatorname{Cov}_{N}(a,m)}{\bar a}
=\frac{N^{-1}\sum_i a_i m_i-\bar a\bar m}{\bar a}
=\frac{\sum_i a_i m_i}{A}-\frac{\sum_i m_i}{N}.
$$

This identity is internal to one fixed panel and one policy. If the panel is
the full candidate menu, zero exposures show exactly how candidate-average FCP
differs from funded-dollar FCP; if it is the positive support, it gives the
selected-count comparison used in the empirical tables. Candidate and funded
coverage coincide exactly only when the corresponding exposure--miss covariance
is zero. The identity does not by itself compare policies with different
supports. It proves the main-text statement and shows why count and dollar
coverage answer distinct questions. With fixed capital $B$, multiplying the
invested-dollar FCP by $A/B$ gives the decision FCP; the remaining share
$1-A/B$ is cash and has no loan-level miss. For an unresolved outcome, the
invested-dollar-minus-count FCP contribution---equivalently, the
count-minus-invested-dollar coverage contribution---has coefficient
$a_i/A-1/N$. Reversing that contrast, count-minus-invested-dollar FCP uses
$1/N-a_i/A$. Likewise, count-minus-fixed-capital FCP uses $1/N-a_i/B$, while the contrast
between two policies (A) and (B) with a common fixed-capital denominator
uses $(a_i^A-a_i^B)/B$ on their support union. Rowwise minimization and
maximization under one shared binary label then follow from Proposition 3. The
bounds are exact within a reporting cell, not jointly across overlapping
policies. The fixed-capital coverage complement is accounting notation; cash
is not itself a conformal observation.

### D.5.3 Monotone worst-catalog completion

<!-- claim:theory.monotone_catalog_completion -->

If $Y\le Y'$ coordinatewise and every fixed-policy loss obeys
$L_j(Y)\le L_j(Y')$, taking a maximum preserves the inequality:

$$
\max_j L_j(Y)\le\max_j L_j(Y').
$$

The all-zero and all-one unresolved vectors are respectively the least and
greatest elements of the binary product order, proving the main-text catalog
bound. Positive-part truncation also preserves
monotonicity. For funded binary-set miscoverage, changing an unresolved label
from zero to one changes the miss indicator by $0$ for empty or full sets, by
$+1$ for a $\{0\}$ singleton, and by $-1$ for a $\{1\}$ singleton. The last
case is why the empirical no-$\{1\}$ catalog gate is required; it is not a
generic property of conformal prediction.

## D.6 Basis-endpoint sufficiency

<!-- claim:theory.basis_endpoint_sufficiency -->

With the full-budget equality, the point-score cap appears in the LP right-hand
side. Suppose the optimal allocation is unique on a cap range, so that $a(c)$ is
single-valued. Within one optimal basis it is then affine in the cap, and against
a fixed guardrail every resolved-outcome contrast is affine. For one unresolved
outcome, the sharp lower contribution is the minimum of two affine functions and
the upper contribution their maximum. The lower bound is concave and the upper
bound convex within the range, so adverse extrema occur at its endpoints.

If an algorithm certifies an exhaustive partition of a cap interval into all
relevant ranges, and uniqueness on each, their endpoints are sufficient for the
sharp interval-wide envelope, up to solver tolerance.

Both hypotheses are stated because neither is established here, and the gap is
material rather than formal. The sharp payoff, default, and miscoverage
contributions are functionals of the allocation, whereas the registered support
audit certifies objective-side facts: for a basic upper-only row with zero dual, a
looser cap retains the incumbent optimum with the same dual certificate and the
same objective value. Under dual degeneracy the objective can remain constant
while the optimal set moves, in which case $a(c)$ is set-valued and "affine in the
cap" has no referent. The audit records primal degeneracy and retains its
scale-aware warnings precisely in order not to claim uniqueness, so this
proposition may not borrow one.

Two further limitations apply to the finite trace. Basis ranging intervals are not
the invariancy intervals of the optimal partition under degeneracy, and distinct
optimal bases at the same cap yield different reported ranges, so a union of basis
intervals is a solver-path-dependent cover rather than a partition. The probe
sequence also warm-starts from the previous basis with presolve enabled, so the
reported widths depend on the traversal order and the solver build. Accordingly
the lineage reports numerical interval coverage of one locked support at a
declared merge tolerance, and claims neither symbolic exactness, nor uniqueness,
nor an exhaustive continuous-path certificate.

For support $\mathcal C$, if $[L(c),U(c)]$ is the paired sharp contrast at cap
$c$, the declared comparator envelope is

$$
\left[\min_{c\in\mathcal C}L(c),
      \max_{c\in\mathcal C}U(c)\right].
$$

This reports whether a sign survives one named outcome-free comparator support.
It is not a causal identified set, a confidence interval, or quantification
over all conceivable comparators.

positive contrast; 96 do so under the zero-tolerance geometric sign. Equal
binary sets therefore do not imply allocation or endpoint-direction invariance
in the declared finite grid. The gamma rows happen to contain no
tolerance-separated opposite sign, but they do not establish a direction beyond
this grid or repair selected- or funded-set validity. All results are
retrospective, post-inspection, and non-confirmatory; no $\theta$, $\gamma$,
ruler, coordinate, window, or policy is selected, and cellwise sharp endpoints
are not asserted jointly attainable across overlapping tracks.

### E.4.4 Complete-candidate-hull score equivalence

<!-- claim:decision.complete_hull_score_equivalence_census -->

The global theorem in Appendix B.5.3 is evaluated on the complete candidate
menu, not on one funded support. For each of the 26 development or primary
months, the audit verifies the affine-hull identity
$\operatorname{aff}(A)=\{a:\mathbf 1^\top a=B\}$ by constructing feasible
difference witnesses under the registered loan and purpose caps. All 26 menus
pass with dimension $n-1$ for $n=6{,}011$--$28{,}106$. Candidate identities,
the 80 set-preservation rows, and closed-calibrator vector hashes replay
exactly. Twenty-six synthetic positive-affine controls pass and 26 deliberately
non-affine controls fail. No outcome or optimizer is read.

| Family and exact subset | Comparisons | Globally equivalent | Not certified equivalent |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| V1d, $\theta=0$ | 1,040 | 1,040 | 0 |
| V1d, $\theta>0,\gamma=0$ | 832 | 832 | 0 |
| V1d, $\theta>0,\gamma>0$ | 3,328 | 0 | 3,328 |
| Closed calibrator pairs, $\gamma=0$ | 1,248 | 0 | 1,248 |
| Closed calibrator pairs, $\gamma>0$ | 4,992 | 0 | 4,992 |

**Table S9M.** Complete full-menu score-equivalence partition. The V1d
equivalences are exactly the identity controls. The minimum failed maximum-
coordinate residual is 0.045261 for V1d and 0.000813 for the calibrator family,
well above their scale-aware numerical tolerances. The cells are a deterministic
overlapping grid rather than independent replications. A failed global
certificate permits but does not force a different allocation at one fixed cap;
it does not identify different optimal faces or optimizer uniqueness. Because
calibrator maps also change the payoff coefficient, their score-only rows do not
establish full optimizer equivalence or non-equivalence.

### E.4.5 Set-native binary robust counterpart

<!-- claim:decision.set_native_robust_counterpart_complete_census -->

The set-native score is zero only for the exact singleton nondefault set and one
for the empty, singleton-default, and two-label sets. Empty sets are assigned one
as an explicit fail-closed convention. Across the 208 repeated
window--role-month menus, the exact taxonomy counts are 52,311 empty,
3,003,924 singleton nondefault, zero singleton default, and 717,965 two-label
memberships. Thus 3,003,924 candidate-window memberships receive score zero and
770,276 receive score one. These counts describe the frozen marginal sets; they
do not establish or inherit a joint-coverage guarantee for their Cartesian
product.

Phase A completes 1,248 outcome-free frontier and solver-audit cells. Its 720
primary portfolios have 78--116 positive exposures (median 92) and exhaust each
USD 1 million budget. Median unresolved exposure share is 0.0070 (maximum
0.1502), median set-risk exposure is 0.0333, and median retained plug-in
objective fraction is 0.6375. Across cells, the sharp standardized-payoff range
has medians -10,286.66 and 10,294.62; the funded-default endpoint medians are
0.349275 and 0.374225; and funded-miscoverage endpoint medians are 0.331350 and
0.359075. These are descriptive portfolio summaries, not probability bounds
induced by the marginal set coverage theorem.

Phase B compares every robust cell to all 25 V1d embedding cells at the same
window, month, ruler, and coordinate. One unresolved binary assignment is shared
loan by loan within each funded-union contrast. The complete direction
partitions are:

| Resolution | Metric | Positive | Negative | Contains zero | Total |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Monthly | Standardized payoff | 5,840 | 9,853 | 2,307 | 18,000 |
| Monthly | Funded default | 13,992 | 2,462 | 1,546 | 18,000 |
| Monthly | Funded binary miscoverage | 11,947 | 4,355 | 1,698 | 18,000 |
| Pooled window | Standardized payoff | 15 | 1,065 | 120 | 1,200 |
| Pooled window | Funded default | 1,196 | 0 | 4 | 1,200 |
| Pooled window | Funded binary miscoverage | 1,009 | 120 | 71 | 1,200 |

**Table S9N (summary view).** The machine-readable 75-row table retains every
$\theta$--$\gamma$ cell and all three metrics, with monthly partitions over 720
comparisons and pooled partitions over 48 comparisons in each row. Positive
payoff is favorable, whereas positive default or miscoverage is adverse. The
pooled default comparison is positive in 45--48 of 48 cells at every fixed
$\theta$--$\gamma$ combination and never negative. No p-value is attached to
these correlated cells, and their sharp endpoints are not jointly attainable
across the grid.

The coarse score cannot distinguish loans within the dominant singleton-
nondefault class, so the plug-in payoff objective and remaining constraints
determine choices within risk-score ties. The nearly
uniform pooled default result coexists with that geometry but does not prove it
as a causal mechanism. The set-native risk coefficient removes one arbitrary
continuous lifting. It provides no evidence of temporal exchangeability and
establishes no joint product-set, selected- or funded-set, or probabilistic
robustness guarantee. No ruler, coordinate, window, embedding, policy, or result is
selected.
