<!-- claim:optimization.finite_rhs_coverage_without_uniqueness -->

The legacy evaluated-cap audit covers 7,297 rows across 15 periods, including
2,204 named unique cap-months. Under its absolute $10^{-7}$ screen, the smallest
absolute nonbasic reduced cost is $3.88\times10^{-4}$; 2,941 reversed-order
reruns yield zero tie-sensitive rows, maximum allocation distance
$1.45\times10^{-14}$, and maximum objective difference $1.72\times10^{-9}$.

The active complete per-solve column-and-row basis audit fresh-solves the same
7,297 rows with
HiGHS/highspy 1.15.1 (native git hash `04024d7`, simplex, presolve on, one
thread). Primal and dual feasibility tolerances are both $10^{-9}$. All
allocations reconcile to the freeze; maximum normalized L1 exposure distance is
$1.13\times10^{-14}$. HiGHS reports the risk row `upper` in 7,228 bases and
`basic` in 69. For an active upper row, its ranging pair is an upper-RHS range.
For a basic slack row with zero multiplier, the same primal--dual certificate
supports the RHS ray from current activity to the domain upper bound. Treating
that basic-row activity range as an active RHS interval is invalid and produces
66 spurious solved-cap failures.

For a structural column, the scale-aware warning screen is
$|\bar c_j|/\max_k|c_k|\le 10^{-7}+10^{-12}$. For a movable row slack, it is
$|\pi_i|/s_i\le 10^{-7}+10^{-12}$ with
$s_i=\max_k|c_k|/\max_k|A_{ik}|$; equality rows are excluded. Allocation
distance is $\lVert a-b\rVert_1/(\sum_i a_i+\sum_i b_i)$, equal to
$\lVert a-b\rVert_1/(2B)$ for two fully invested solutions, and its registered
difference threshold is $10^{-10}$. Conditional probes allow objective loss
$\max\{10^{-7},10^{-12}\max(1,|z^\star|)\}$ dollars.

After this status-aware correction, all 7,297 central intervals contain their
solved cap but leave 196 positive gaps over $[0.05,0.12]$, with maximum width
0.001477. The status-aware recovery re-solves in fresh HiGHS sessions all 196
retrospectively registered midpoint seeds. Every basis, dual-sign,
objective, feasibility, seed-containment, and
target-gap gate passes; their union leaves no gap above $10^{-10}$ in any of the
15 periods. Bilateral breakpoint paths have zero allocation
differences above $10^{-10}$ (maximum $3.08\times10^{-14}$), so the corrected
same-cap mobility cooccurrence count is zero.
At zero merge tolerance, 465 machine-precision seams remain, with maximum width
$1.67\times10^{-16}$; none remains at $10^{-15}$. This is why the coverage
statement is numerical rather than symbolic exactness.

The stricter scale-aware screen nevertheless records 13 basis warnings at eight
cap-variable targets and one midpoint warning that repeats a registered target
at both neighboring endpoints. All reduced costs retain the expected
sign. The eight conditional programs use an epsilon-near-optimal objective band
and move any one exposure by at most USD 0.962; this is not evidence of an
exactly distinct optimum. Numerical support coverage therefore passes without
promoting a numerical-uniqueness claim; the warnings prove neither numerical
nor exact nonuniqueness. No exact symbolic face, global face
diameter, allocation continuity, seam conditioning, or continuous-joint-
frontier uniqueness claim is made.

## E.7 Why no policy is promoted

The empirical record does not support a winner. First, all 40 finite-archive
candidate-coverage bounds exclude 0.90 before optimization, and 31 of 40 cell
reference tail areas meet the separate joint-block diagnostic's locked nominal
reporting thresholds. Those facts withhold a transferred conformal deployment
certificate; by themselves they do not rank policies under another estimand.
The decision-ranking evidence is instead that the endpoint sign changes across
the two rulers and three coordinates, while named comparators disagree and
endpoint envelopes over the finite registered cap values spanning
$[0.05,0.12]$ eliminate all one-sided directions without computing
continuous-support extrema, and all W8
development-support directions. Selecting .25, one ruler, an earlier window,
one comparator, or one of the six payoff cells after seeing these results would
convert a specification audit into post-result selection.

# Appendix F: Reproducibility and Active Lineage

## F.1 Two-phase execution

The active audit uses two immutable phases. Phase 1 produces learner scores,
residual recipes, label-availability audits, outcome-free geometry, LP solve
records, allocations, and comparator supports. Before writing a freeze it
verifies full budgets, solver status, split-conformal ranks, label retention,
C2 moment matching, exact IDs, and the absence of outcome columns.

Phase 2 verifies the freeze descriptors, reconstructs the endpoint panel, and
performs exact keyed joins without changing a score, recipe, support, ruler,
coordinate, or allocation. The active primary evaluation contains 1,408
coverage rows, 5,112 monthly evaluations, 360 aggregates, 221,040 paired sharp
contrasts, and 648 comparator envelopes. Separate complete families cover five
credit learners, endpoint lag, portfolio structure, missingness encoding, and
a second temporal origin. The evidence builder checks hashes, contracts, and
cardinalities before producing 43 tables, five figure families in PNG and PDF,
and one paper-facing manifest. Additional outcome-isolated families cover joint
fit-label completion, deterministic allocation granularity, marginal score and
residual-distribution diagnostics, complete-catalog transport, and funded
estimand dependence, plus the set-preserving continuous-embedding and closed
CatBoost calibrator-family sensitivities, the complete-hull score certificate,
and the set-native binary counterpart with declared empty-set fail-closure.

## F.2 Replay contract

The replay contract distinguishes two operations. **Publication replay** runs
the current builder against immutable DVC artifacts, verifies every descriptor,
and regenerates paper tables, figures, and the manifest transactionally.
**Scientific replay** checks out the recorded protocol commit for a lineage and
uses the `uv.lock` hash stored with that lineage; current source code is not
silently substituted for historical scientific code.

For the calibrator sensitivity, the exact annotated four-stage chain is
protocol P $\rightarrow$ outcome-free artifact A $\rightarrow$ evaluation lock
B $\rightarrow$ evaluated artifact C. A is the single direct child of P, B of
A, and C of B. The source registry and editor-only reproducibility crosswalk
bind the exact tags and commits; those identifiers are provenance gates, not
empirical claims.

The complete-hull lineage uses an annotated protocol commit followed by one
direct-child six-output artifact commit. The set-native lineage uses the stricter
four-state chain Phase-A protocol $P_1\rightarrow$ outcome-free artifact
$A_1\rightarrow$ hash-pinned Phase-B protocol $P_2\rightarrow$ evaluated
artifact $B_1$, with every arrow a single-parent direct-child relationship.
Neither lineage changes a protected historical artifact.

The shared contract requires:

1. a lineage-specific environment locked by `uv`;
2. immutable, hash-described outcome-free and evaluated roots tracked by 53
   DVC pointers across the primary audit, two-ruler diagnostic, credit controls,
   endpoint, structure, missingness, individual-age second-origin, fit-label
   completion, allocation-granularity, joint-block rank-reference diagnostic, and
   label-Mondrian, and policy-support optimal-face/RHS-recovery families; plus
   nine hash-described scientific Git artifact lineages: five direct-child
   bundles for the V8 common-panel response, V3I marginal gap,
   residual-distribution frontier, decision catalog, and funded-estimand audit,
   plus the set-preserving embedding's protocol-to-source-to-evaluation
   direct-child chain and the calibrator sensitivity's
   protocol-to-source-to-evaluation-lock-to-result chain, the complete-hull
   direct-child certificate, and the set-native four-stage phase chain, each
   verified against its exact registered path set;
3. a separate freeze and evaluate command with no combined shortcut;
4. exact ID alignment at the outcome join;
5. byte-identical evidence builds;
6. claim-sync tests across the manifest, body, supplement, and generated TeX;
7. full tests, lint, static typing, protected-artifact validation, and an
   active implementation/evidence drift gate; and
8. compilation and page-level visual inspection of the body, supplement, and
   official IJDS submission PDF.

Protected historical stages and their extraction manifest are not required to
replay the active evidence and are not overwritten.

## F.3 Anonymous-review boundary

At the eventual anonymous-review freeze, exact commits, tags, hashes,
repository links, and remote coordinates must move out of reviewer artifacts
because they are searchable author fingerprints; the editor-only registry
preserves that crosswalk. The current pre-freeze source retains the calibrator
chain above for scientific integration and is therefore not the final anonymous
supplement. Any release at acceptance is conditional on human confirmation of
acquisition and redistribution rights, resolution of journal-license
compatibility, and remediation of the public repository/Pages anonymity leak.
Only after those conditions are satisfied may the code, environment lock,
evidence manifest, permitted immutable pointers, and lawful reconstruction
instructions be released under the journal's data and code policy.

## G.1 Prospective designs that would answer different questions

The following designs are future contracts, not reanalyses authorized on the
inspected archive.

| Target estimand | First viable design | Required validity bridge | Stop condition |
|---|---|---|---|
| Marginal coverage of one future loan | Freeze chronology, score, taxonomy, temporal weights, and one nonexchangeable-conformal theorem before the target outcome | An external, independent, or design-based upper bound on the theorem's swap, decoupling, or dependence penalty, with any confidence-bound failure probability propagated | The penalty is unbounded, postselected, or vacuous, or its estimation failure probability is omitted; current KS-like distances, PSI, rolling origins, and joint-block flags cannot substitute for it |
| Selection-conditional coverage and FCR | JOMI with exactly $K$ selected loans and equal exposure $B/K$ [@jin2025focal] | Same-population exchangeability or a proved replacement, permutation-equivariant selection, disjoint policy construction and final calibration, and complete reference sets | Calibration-row permutations or irrelevant ID reversals change the rule, reference sets are too small, or historical target outcomes influence the policy |
| Expected fractional exposure-weighted FCP | Exactly $K$ positive exposures, $A=\sum_j a_j>0$, and a predeclared hard concentration bound $a_i/A\le\kappa/K$ | Count FCR calibrated at $\alpha/\kappa$, using the deterministic inequality $\operatorname{FCP}^{\$}\le\kappa\operatorname{FCP}^{N}$ | $\kappa$ is selected post hoc, the portfolio denominator is ambiguous, the bound is written relative to $B$ while cash makes $A<B$, or the adjusted sets are uninformative |
| Next-month portfolio decision risk | Complete issue month as the sampling unit, complete eligible endpoints, bounded loss, and a policy family frozen before risk calibration | Classical CRC for an exchangeable monotone family with its finite-sample safe-terminal correction; stability-based CRC for a symmetric non-monotone algorithm only with a valid nonvacuous stability certificate; or LTT for a finite reoptimized catalog evaluated on valid contexts [@angelopoulos2024risk; @angelopoulos2026nonmonotonic; @angelopoulos2025ltt] | Too few valid blocks, temporal assumptions fail, an eligible endpoint is incomplete, the classical CRC correction, non-monotone stability/reference-risk margin, or LTT multiplicity contract fails, or a favorable policy is selected after outcomes |

In the first row, *temporal weights* means the sampling weights required by a
named nonexchangeable or covariate-shift conformal theorem
[@barber2023beyond; @tibshirani2019covshift]. They must be frozen without
target labels and accompanied by the theorem's discrepancy or likelihood-ratio
contract. They are not the optimized dollar exposures in the third row.

These routes control different objects. Expected FCR is not a
high-probability bound on one realized portfolio, a block-loss guarantee is not
loan-level coverage, and residual cash changes the fixed-capital versus
invested-capital denominator. Predictive programming, multi-variable
prediction-set design, and catalog-uniform decision calibration remain
additional designs under their own independent-calibration and sampling
contracts [@zhao2024cpp; @lutzow2026mcp;
@shekhar2026decision_calibrated_pacing].

The study uses one discontinued consumer-credit platform and accepted 36-month
loans only. It observes no outcomes for rejected applicants and therefore no
approval or reject-inference counterfactuals.
The terminal label compresses payment paths and competing events into one
binary endpoint. The status-indexed payoff proxy omits timing, recovery, fees,
discounting,
and capital costs. The temporal gap does not restore exchangeability. Numeric
logistic, monotonic CatBoost, and both WOE/IV learners are coverage controls,
not four additional portfolio systems.

The raw archive also contains 60-month contracts, duration-censored cohorts,
and 48 late-schema fields. Including them would change the target or temporal
information set. The controls share one platform and their OOT differences
cannot support promotion because the same outcomes define this audit.

Platform grade, subgrade, rate, and installment are observable at the investor
timestamp but endogenous to historical underwriting and pricing policy; the
active contract excludes known post-origin servicing variables, so this is a
policy-portability limit rather than a claim of post-origin leakage.

The archive is not a verified historical snapshot. Servicing dates after the
cutoff require a conservative reconstruction that cannot recover the missing
point-in-time extract. The six-month Charged Off delay is a modeling assumption
rather than an observed operational date. The retrospectively locked fit-label
analysis supports only lags satisfying strict greater-than-99% retention; the
separate endpoint analysis has one upper-coverage exception at 12 months. They
were not crossed factorially. Delinquency recency is structurally nullable and
bankruptcy count has partial early schema support; deterministic frozen
mappings and two alternative encodings are evaluated, but the missingness
mechanism is not identified. The second origin remains a retrospective
recurrence from the same platform, not prospective validation.

The combined-rank diagnostic was locked only after the archive, the 40 sharp
exclusions, and an exploratory flag pattern had been inspected. Its Holm
cutoffs are nominal reporting thresholds, not post-selection or study-wide
FWER control. A nonflag in nine cells does not verify the assumption, and a
flag of the stronger joint-block null does not directly refute the usual
one-future-point condition. Label-Mondrian requires exchangeability within each score-stratum
and class, which is not established, and its much larger two-label sets expose
a material efficiency cost.

The observed-only fit and three declared stress rules retain the coverage
conclusion but not one common geometric path. The all-default scenario removes
the W7--W8 crossing, and the four nonlinear refits are not exhaustive over
every missing-label assignment. The declared USD 25 floor-with-cash
transformation changes 2,985 positive exposures and shifts the evaluated rates
by at most 0.001284 percentage points; it does not reoptimize or define a
mixed-integer policy.

Candidate-level coverage is not selected-set coverage. C2 matches one funded
point-score moment but neither equalizes feasible sets nor defines an
independently specified counterfactual. Purpose categories and score strata are not protected classes,
so the audit is not a fair-lending assessment. The overlapping windows are not
independent evidence. Exact mirror-sample geometry identifies each frozen
threshold, while the two-threshold identity accounts for coverage changes through
crossed target mass; neither is a universal low-bin or transport result.

The two-ruler diagnostic contains three interior coordinates, not a continuous
joint frontier. Coordinate one is a structural null only for the plug-in
objective-value contrast; allocation and outcome contrasts require uniqueness
or reuse of the same optimizer. Objective matching uses a
model-implied payoff, while normalized-score matching does not equalize its
opportunity cost. These are coupled chronological contexts without an
independent selection/recalibration split, complete decision outcomes, or a
compatible iid/exchangeability contract. They therefore do not satisfy the
conditions needed to import a CROMS, inverse conformal risk-control, or
decision-calibration guarantee.

The active conclusion is deliberately narrow. In the CatBoost stratum selected
after inspection solely for illustration,
the fitted threshold and binary-set composition change sharply across the final
two calibration blocks, but that path is not invariant to every fit-label completion and
does not generalize to all score bins. All 40 sharp
finite-archive coverage bounds exclude 0.90; 31 of 40 joint-block cell reference
tail areas meet the separate diagnostic's locked nominal reporting thresholds without a post-selection FWER
claim; and label conditioning
produces a mixed, less efficient sensitivity rather than a uniform repair.
Status-indexed portfolio direction changes with the declared ruler,
coordinate, residual recipe, and registered comparator support. No selected
gamma, ruler, coordinate, policy, causal effect, prospective guarantee,
selected-set validity, exhaustive continuous point-cap certificate, Markov
certificate, universal guardrail direction, or deployment
recommendation is claimed.

# Appendix H: Closest-Work Positioning

CRPTO combines established ingredients but asks a different identification
question. The matrix below records the boundary that is summarized in the main
paper; it is positioning evidence, not an empirical result or novelty claim for
credit scoring, conformal prediction, or linear programming separately.

| Literature family | Established contribution | Active CRPTO boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Finite-batch and sample-conditional split conformal [@marques2025universal; @duchi2025sampleconditional] | Exact Beta--Binomial empirical-coverage law for a shared threshold, and high-probability sample-/group-conditional guarantees under iid sampling | Uses the complementary law only as a stronger joint-block retrospective reference with tie-safe domination and unresolved completion; the chronological archive does not inherit iid sample-conditional guarantees |
| Probability scaling, beta calibration, and Venn--Abers prediction [@platt2000; @zadrozny2002; @kull2017; @vovk2014] | Logistic, isotonic, and beta probability maps plus a distinct multiprobabilistic calibration construction under their respective sampling contracts | Reports a closed four-map CatBoost sensitivity under one common uncalibrated-probability ($q_{\mathrm{raw}}$) taxonomy: 18/32 pooled upper endpoints are below 0.90, so a uniform family-wide shortfall is not established. It selects no map, transfers no Venn guarantee to $p^\prime$, and runs no alternative-map portfolio optimization |
| Covariate-shift weighted conformal prediction [@tibshirani2019covshift] | Reweights calibration examples by a source-to-target likelihood ratio to obtain marginal target-distribution coverage under an invariant conditional outcome law | The active design neither prespecifies nor validates the required ratio and conditional-invariance ingredients; LP exposure weights and date decay are not conformal sampling weights |
| Credit scoring and cost-aware calibration [@lessmann2015; @yang2025costaware; @das2023creditgraph] | Probability quality and richer predictive structure | Treats a Platt-scaled default score as an input; no AUC-leadership claim |
| P2P and robust credit portfolios [@serrano2016profitscoring; @chi2019p2p; @babaei2020p2p] | Economic loan selection under risk and uncertainty | Adds binary-set geometry, outcome isolation, and comparator identification |
| Classwise and nonexchangeable conformal prediction [@ding2023; @oliveira2024split; @gibbs2024online] | Label-category calibration and guarantees under explicit discrepancy, dependence, concentration, or feedback designs | Audits a retrospective label-Mondrian sensitivity but establishes neither within-class temporal exchangeability nor an online-feedback guarantee |
| Joint-batch and dependent-sequence conformal prediction [@gazin2025batch; @barber2026timeseries] | Joint label-vector sets under iid sampling and, for the paper's symmetric combining rules, class-conditional sampling; plus sharp coverage-loss bounds for stationary beta-mixing sequences | The combined-rank statistic is a diagnostic rather than a joint batch prediction set; issue-month menus do not identify a stationary sequence or mixing coefficient |
| Censoring-aware and competing-risk prediction [@candes2023survival; @gui2024adaptive; @li2023online_loans] | Lower prediction bounds for time-to-event outcomes under explicit censoring contracts, and event-specific default/prepayment modeling | Uses a partially identified terminal binary label; it has neither exact event/censoring times nor a competing-risk estimand, overlap audit, or funded-set guarantee |
| Conformal portfolio and contextual optimization [@kato2025; @sun2024ptc; @johnstone2021; @patel2024; @hu2026crc] | Per-candidate conformal intervals used to rank portfolios, conformal or coverage-calibrated uncertainty sets for contextual robust optimization, and direct decision-risk or robustness calibration | Audits a frozen binary credit score, endpoint reconstruction, and matched comparators; no post-selection asset-return, contextual-LP, or selected-set guarantee is inherited |
| Selection-conditional coverage and false-coverage-rate control [@jin2025focal; @gazin2025informative] | Validity targets tailored to black-box or informative selection under their own reference-set and multiplicity contracts | Candidate-level coverage is not transferred to budget-selected loans; neither procedure is implemented by the monthly optimizer |
| Chance-constrained conformal predictive programming [@zhao2024cpp] | Calibrates a constraint-function quantile; its general a-posteriori guarantee uses a second i.i.d. calibration sample and covers an offset event | CRPTO inserts a prediction-set endpoint as an LP coefficient; no funded-set, zero-threshold, or temporal-transport certificate transfers |
| Decision-optimal and counterfactual prediction sets [@wang2026optimal_decision_prediction_sets; @zheng2026counterfactual_decision_sets] | Couple set construction or coverage to an explicit downstream loss or induced action | Audits an observational accepted-loan archive; no counterfactual funding effect or policy-coupled validity |
| Utility-directed and learned decision-aware conformal sets [@cortesgomez2025utility; @yeh2026; @chen2026polyhedral_conformal_ro] | Incorporate downstream utility into classification-set construction, or learn conditional/polyhedral uncertainty-set geometry against robust decision loss with their own calibration or independent recalibration contracts | Freezes one binary-set lifting instead of learning the predictive object; it lacks those design/recalibration splits and inherits none of their downstream robustness guarantees |

**Table S13A.** Closest-work boundary for predictive, transport, and selection
methods.

<div style="page-break-before: always;"></div>

| Literature family | Established contribution | Active CRPTO boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Multi-variable conformal set design [@lutzow2026mcp] | Jointly optimizes prediction-set shape and calibration through scenario optimization; RemMCP provides expected coverage under exchangeability and optimizer regularity, with a dimension-dependent calibration cost | MCP adds an explicit set-design objective and a new algorithm; CRPTO instead audits the endpoint of a fixed binary set and inherits no MCP certificate for temporal transport or the selected credit portfolio |
| Catalog-uniform decision-calibrated conformal pacing [@shekhar2026decision_calibrated_pacing] | Calibrates the support function of forecast errors over a finite policy-sensitivity catalog and selects a robust pacing policy under exchangeable blocks, affine effects, and simultaneous catalog-wide uncertainty contracts | Their method uses neither a binary label set nor a set-equivalent per-loan endpoint; CRPTO's chronological archive does not establish those contracts and inherits no selected-policy or funded-loan coverage guarantee |
| Valid selection and decision-risk calibration [@hegazy2025valid_selection_conformal_sets; @bao2025croms; @yeh2025training; @zhou2026creme] | Stability for selection among conformal sets (Hegazy et al.), conformal-risk model selection in CRO (Bao et al.), optimized-certainty-equivalent/tail-risk training (Yeh et al.), and expected miscoverage--regret assessment with split recalibration after selection (Zhou and Zhu) | Uses ruler sensitivity as a diagnostic; its coupled chronological contexts lack an independent selection/recalibration split, complete decision outcomes, and a compatible iid/exchangeability contract |
| Decision calibration [@zhao2021decisioncalibration; @shekhar2026decision_calibrated_pacing] | Makes predictions indistinguishable to a declared decision class, or calibrates policy impacts uniformly over a finite catalog under its own block assumptions | Probability, conformal, and risk calibration in CRPTO are different objects; no decision-indistinguishability or catalog-uniform certificate is inherited |
| Decision-focused learning with uncertain constraints [@donti2017; @elmachtoub2022; @liu2021riskbounds; @schutte2024robust; @im2025spor; @mandi2024] | Trains predictions or robust surrogates against downstream decision loss; SPO-RC adds feasibility-sensitive learning with contextual uncertainty sets for uncertain constraints | Preserves the predictor for governance and audits a post-hoc decision layer; it claims neither regret/Fisher consistency nor the SPO-RC constraint guarantee |
| Decision-value attribution [@ziliaskopoulos2026dva] | Uses Shapley games to attribute realized or predicted downstream decision value to information sources, operational design parameters, and their interactions in a fixed prediction--optimization system | CRPTO does not attribute value to features; it certifies score-order equivalence, comparator support, and sharp outcome direction for declared pipeline variants |
| Smart PtRO and learned predictive ambiguity sets [@caunhye2026smartptro; @guo2026lpas] | Recent preprints learn against covariate perturbations or produce contextual scenario distributions and Wasserstein radii using decision loss and calibration objectives | These are prospective algorithmic redesigns under different perturbation/data contracts; CRPTO's nonempty-set worst-label rule with declared empty-set fail-closure is a retrospective marginal-set audit and inherits neither certificate nor reported performance |
| CRPTO comparator-design principle | Holding the decision problem fixed while changing one ingredient | Shows that a shared numeric cap does not hold decision stringency fixed |
